h: Witton Park and the Wider Blackburn Patch
p: Blackburn's treetop course sits in Witton Country Park on the west side of town, a big green space with woodland, open fields and the River Darwen running through it. That setting matters, because it means the day doesn't have to end when you unclip. There's room to kick a ball about, walk the riverside paths or just flop on the grass with a flask and some butties.

Timing-wise, think of the course as a half-day job. Between kitting up, the practice run and getting yourselves round, a couple of hours disappears fast, and if your group includes a ditherer on the first platform (there's always one), add a bit more. Eat something before you start; climbing on an empty stomach is no fun.
Spectators who don't fancy the heights can usually follow along on foot below for a good chunk of it, which is half the entertainment for grandparents with a camera.

Around the town, there's more to fill the afternoon. Blackburn Cathedral sits right in the centre, Ewood Park is a must for Rovers fans, and the Leeds and Liverpool Canal towpath makes an easy, flat stroll. If you've still got energy, the climb to Darwen Tower on the moors above neighbouring Darwen gives you huge Lancashire views, and the Ribble Valley, with Clitheroe and its little castle, is only a short drive north.
